summary: Completed backend API and browser E2E testing for customer booking, lookup, auth, admin queue, confirmation, availability, and duplicate protection.

issues: Uses native HTML date and select controls rather than the specified Shadcn-style Calendar/Select components; controls vary by browser and mobile screenshot shows browser-native date picker affordance.
No footer is rendered despite the design specification requiring a deep route-blue footer with brand/contact/service links.

action_items: Restrict CORS allow_origin_regex from .* to explicit configured frontend origins when credentials are enabled.
Add brute-force lockout/rate limiting after five failed authentication attempts as required by the auth playbook.
Replace native date/select controls with the requested accessible component primitives and add the specified customer footer.
critical_code_review_comments: CORS currently allows every origin while allow_credentials=True, which can expose credentialed auth requests to arbitrary origins; use an explicit environment-driven allowlist.
Authentication has no failed-attempt counter or lockout implementation, leaving the password endpoint brute-forceable.
seed_data_creation: Created two TEST API/browser bookings in the shared demo database; both were used for lifecycle verification and remain as booking queue records.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Core customer and admin workflows pass against the public URL. Retest CORS/auth hardening and verify native controls/footer after fixes.
rca of the issue: Security gaps are visible directly in server.py: CORSMiddleware uses allow_origin_regex='.*' with credentials, and login only verifies bcrypt without tracking failed attempts. UI gaps are in App.js where Availability uses input type=date/select and no footer component exists.
